title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 6
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: A tank holds 960 litres. A quarter is drawn off, then a third of what remains. How much is left?
questions.explanation: After the first draw 720 litres remain; removing a third of that leaves 480. Subtracting the fractions of the original gives 400, which applies the second fraction to the wrong quantity.

questions.prompt: A lorry travelling at 60 km/h has a 24 km head start. A van sets off along the same road at 78 km/h. How long before the van catches the lorry?
questions.explanation: The van gains 18 km every hour, so it closes the 24 km gap in 24/18 = 1.3 hours. Dividing by the van's own speed ignores that the lorry keeps moving.

questions.prompt: An account earned £1,449.00 in simple interest over 3.5 years at 4.6% a year. What was the principal?
questions.explanation: Interest is principal × rate × years, so the principal is £1,449.00 / (0.046 × 3.5) = £9,000.00. Omitting the years gives £31,500.00.

questions.prompt: Eight readings are 7, 11, 11, 14, 19, 19, 19, 31. What is the difference between the mode and the range?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value, 19; the range is 31 − 7 = 24. The difference is 5. Reporting the mode or the range alone is the trap.

questions.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of 12 cm and 18 cm, 7 cm apart. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area is the mean of the parallel sides times the distance between them: (12 + 18)/2 × 7 = 105 square centimetres.

questions.prompt: A floor measuring 372 cm by 300 cm is to be covered exactly by identical square tiles, as large as possible. How many tiles are needed?
questions.explanation: The largest square that divides both sides is the highest common factor of 372 and 300, which is 12 cm. The floor takes 31 × 25 = 775 tiles.

questions.prompt: Of 45 customers who bought a printer, 18 also bought ink. What percentage of printer buyers bought ink?
questions.explanation: 18 out of 45 is 40%. The figures 18 and 45 are counts, not percentages, and dividing the wrong way round gives 250%.

questions.prompt: An item was sold for £391.00 at a loss of 15% on its cost. What was the cost?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 85% of cost, so the cost is £391.00 / 0.85 = £460.00. Adding 15% to the sale price gives £449.65, applying the percentage to the wrong base.

questions.prompt: Tea costing £4.20 a kilogram is blended with tea costing £7.40 a kilogram to give a blend worth £5.00 a kilogram. In what ratio are they mixed?
questions.explanation: The cheaper tea is £0.80 below the blend price and the dearer is £2.40 above it. The quantities are in inverse proportion to those gaps: 2.4 : 0.8, or 3 : 1.

questions.prompt: A sequence starts at 5 and increases by 7 each term. Which term equals 152?
questions.explanation: Solve 5 + (k − 1) × 7 = 152: (k − 1) = 21, so k = 22. Forgetting the offset gives 21.

questions.prompt: 9 workers complete a job in 20 days. At the same rate, how long would 12 workers take?
questions.explanation: The job is 180 worker-days, so 12 workers take 180/12 = 15 days. Scaling the wrong way gives 27 days, which is longer despite more workers.

questions.prompt: A cost was estimated at £3,910.00 but turned out to be £3,400.00. By what percentage did the estimate exceed the actual cost?
questions.explanation: The excess is £510.00, which as a percentage of the actual cost is 15%. Dividing by the estimate instead gives 13%.

questions.prompt: A jar costs £2.30, or three for £5.85. How much is saved by buying three in the offer rather than singly?
questions.explanation: Three singly cost £6.90; the offer costs £5.85. The saving is £1.05. The per-jar saving is £0.35, which is the distractor.

questions.prompt: Ten scores have a mean of 63. A score of 41 is replaced by one of 81. What is the new mean?
questions.explanation: The total rises by 81 − 41 = 40, so the mean rises by 4: from 63 to 67. Adding the whole difference to the mean gives 103.

questions.prompt: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular twelve-sided polygon?
questions.explanation: The interior angles total (12 − 2) × 180 = 1800 degrees, so each is 150 degrees. The exterior angle is 30 degrees.

questions.prompt: A recipe for six people uses 450 g of flour. How much is needed for fifteen people?
questions.explanation: Per person the recipe uses 75 g, so fifteen people need 1,125 g.

questions.prompt: Successive discounts of 20% and 15% are applied to a price. What single discount is equivalent?
questions.explanation: The price is multiplied by 0.80 × 0.85 = 0.68, a reduction of 32%. Adding the discounts gives 35%, which double counts the overlap.

questions.prompt: A car can travel 480 km on a full tank. Starting with a full tank, how many refuelling stops are needed for a journey of 1,750 km?
questions.explanation: The car covers 480 km, then 960, then 1,440 km after two stops, and 1,920 km after three — enough for 1,750 km. So 3 stops are needed, one fewer than the number of tanks used.

questions.prompt: At what number of years does a sum double under simple interest at 8% a year?
questions.explanation: Simple interest adds 8% of the original each year, so doubling needs 100/8 = 12.5 years. Under compound interest it would take about 9 years, which is the distractor.

questions.prompt: Six pumps empty a tank in 14 hours. How long would 21 pumps of the same type take?
questions.explanation: The work is 84 pump-hours, so 21 pumps take 84/21 = 4 hours. More pumps must mean less time, so any answer above 14 hours is wrong.

questions.prompt: In how many distinct orders can the letters of a six-letter word be arranged if exactly two of the letters are identical and the rest are different?
questions.explanation: Six distinct letters would give 720 orders, but swapping the two identical letters produces no new arrangement, so divide by 2: 360.
